- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.53) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or mean.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative (0.18–0.36) and recent price is falling; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment drag.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong moves; apply a 1–3% downward bias if price deviates >3σ from 14-day moving average.
- When sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.09–0.18), model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for sentiment-induced weakness.
